result.title: CFBrainAug: Modularity-Induced Counterfactual Brain Network Augmentation for Interpretable fMRI-based Autism Diagnosis
result.summary: Machine learning on resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) brain networks is promising for diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), but existing methods are prone to overfitting on limited training data, and their post-hoc statistical attribution offers limited clinical interpretability. We propose CFBrainAug, a counterfactual brain network learning framework that unifies data augmentation and counterfactual explanation by learning label-altered brain networks. Unlike conventional label-preserving augmentation, CFBrainAug first retrieves a label-opposite yet topologically similar candidate and then refines it under a module-number constraint. Jointly training on factual and counterfactual networks enriches the training distribution around the decision boundary, enabling a lightweight feature-selection-based SVM to perform competitively with recent graph deep learning methods. Meanwhile, the counterfactuals provide intrinsic explanations by identifying the connectivity differences between each subject and its counterfactual. Experiments on the ABIDE I dataset show that CFBrainAug reaches an accuracy of 74.1% on the NYU site, suggesting that counterfactual augmentation can complement more complex models in small-sample brain network analysis.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 CFBrainAug，通过检索并模块数约束精修「标签相反但拓扑相似」的脑网络，把反事实样本与真实样本联合训练，并用二者的连接差异给出内在解释，用于小样本 fMRI 自闭症诊断。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「标签翻转的反事实样本＋差异即解释」思路可能为 LVR 中的反事实监督、证据筛选与贡献分配提供概念类比，但属脑网络分类任务，能否迁移到多模态 latent 推理仍需核查。
